doc: The match camera (CamRig, scripts/match/cam.gd). match_hunter_scale: how many times bigger every match Hunter is drawn on top of Hunter.VIS_SCALE's base 1.12 (visual only; farm, Model Room and Bokidex never use it; hitboxes, speeds and ranges keep their size). styles: the Settings 'Camera' presets: pitch in degrees down from level, dist m back from the focus, fov the vertical lens in degrees, rise m the view aims above the focus. hunter_scale (source_scale only, off unless picked): match Hunters drawn that many times bigger (on top of Hunter.VIS_SCALE, which already holds match_hunter_scale: 1.91 x 1.232 = the 2.35x total the test style was tuned at; hitboxes and hit circles keep their size), so this style shows the source's ground across and its Hunter size together (docs/MOVEMENT_FEEL.md 'Source scale flag'); the home keeps the default style under it. follow: the Settings 'Camera follow' cursor lean: [deadzone, share or maxzone, cap m, ease 1/s, quadratic easing]; lean reads the cursor's distance from you in metres (deadzone m, share of the distance past it), the others its distance from the screen centre (-1..1). lean_edge_m: metres the cursor lean and an aimed cast keep between you and the screen's edge. pose_far_m: metres (flat) from the camera's focus past which a Hunter on screen is posed every 2nd frame (SimLod.pose_every): past the play view at zoom 1, small at a wide one. source: the bands docs/MOVEMENT_FEEL.md 'Camera framing vs the source' measured from the source footage; --cam-framing-check holds the default style inside them (pitch, lens, feet, and start_arm_m: the arm at the wheel's start notch) and the source_scale style inside across_m; --move-feel-check holds its medium Hunter inside hunter_screen_pct.. scout: the held far look (ScoutLook, Settings 'Look ahead'): ease_in_s / ease_out_s seconds the view takes to go 90% of the way out toward the cursor and back, zoom how much wider it gets held (0.25: 25%, the sight's share, so the lean has room up and down too), sight_mul how much further you see inside a cone_deg cone along your aim while it is held (walking speed unchanged). source: the bands docs/MOVEMENT_FEEL.md 'Camera framing vs the source' measured from the source footage; --cam-framing-check holds the default style inside them (pitch, lens, feet, and start_arm_m: the arm at the wheel's start notch) and the source_scale style inside across_m; --move-feel-check holds its medium Hunter inside hunter_screen_pct. frame_aspect: width / height of the screen the styles' fov is measured on (16:9, the source's frame): other screen shapes get the same ground across (CamRig.frame_fov), held by --camera-frame-check.

farm.doc: The farm's close third-person view (FarmCam, scripts/home/farm_cam.gd). third_person: false puts the top-down Settings view back in the farm, nothing else to change. pitch_deg: degrees down from level (a right-drag tips it between pitch_min_deg and pitch_max_deg). dist_min..dist_max: metres behind the aim point at the mouse wheel's closest and widest (look_out: the most Ctrl's wide look may go past the widest, as a share of that range). fov: the vertical lens, rise: metres above your feet the view aims at. orbit_per_px: radians a right-drag turns per pixel. wall_gap: metres the camera keeps off the ground and walls (it is pulled in along the view, but never closer than wall_min_m while tipping steeper, up to wall_pitch_deg, can keep that distance: no face filling the screen); props: [half width, height, half depth] in metres of what stands off the tile grid and counts as a wall for the camera (the portal ring and the glider rack, at the home's spots); building_m and tree_m: how tall a building (its roof also reaches ~0.8 m past its tile) and a tree count as for that (the placed block under them is only as high as you can climb). game_pitch_deg and game_dist_mul: while a Boki minigame is on, the view tips up to at least that angle and draws back that many times, so the court shows; blend_s: seconds to turn between this view and the top-down one (build mode and the training sessions use that).

pan.doc: The default cursor pan (follow 'pan'), numbers from the target feel's data: deadzone 0.1 and maxzone 0.9 of the half-screen, quadratic easing, 100% pan distance. Its follow row is [deadzone, maxzone, up m, spring omega rad/s, quadratic]: up = how far the view slides with the cursor at the top edge; omega = sqrt(766.7), the critically damped spring of spring power 5 (constant lerp(100, 1600, (power - 1) / 9)). side_m: the same at the left or right edge; down_m: at the bottom edge. The slide is an ellipse of those three reaches and never takes you or your plate off screen (CamRig._cast_room). The data's hysteresis band (0.225 / 0.325) has no stated meaning here and is not used.

trail.doc: The camera's follow across the ground [footage: briefs/hero-ref/dredge.md 4 and 8, ostra.md 2-3, mooshmoosh.md 2; 50 px = 1 m]. Each frame the view closes on you at min(follow_rate x gap, sqrt(2 x catch_decel x gap)) m/s: a run keeps it ~0.35 m behind and stopped with you in ~0.2 s, and a dash leaves it behind, then it eases in at a steady deceleration (Grimble's 4.6 m dash in 0.12 s: the pan peaks ~700 px/s, is down to ~300 px/s at 0.3 s and stops by ~0.5 s; ~0.4 s for a blink). follow_rate (1/s): the tight part, near you. catch_decel (m/s^2): fitted to that pan. max_gap (m): the furthest it may trail, just over the source dash's own ~3.2 m gap, so a long 40 m/s Wirerun can't take you off screen. cut_speed (m/s): a move faster than this in one frame is a teleport, and the view cuts to it, as the source does on Motley's Lantern Trade.

zoom.doc: The wheel's zoom (CamWheel, scripts/match/cam_wheel.gd), as a factor on the style's distance. min/max/step/ctrl are the farm's (the farm camera is untouched). match: the match's own range, from the target feel's data. Its camera arm runs 20.2..30.2 m in 4 notches of 2.5 m (a 59 degree HORIZONTAL lens, 35.3 vertical at 16:9: 34.2 m of ground across at the widest, 22.9 m at the closest). The default style has the data's lens (35.3 vertical, 11-26; it was 32 with the arm stretched x1.1098 to show the same ground), so 1 m of the data's arm is 1 m of ours and the factors are 20.2 / 23 -> min, 30.2 / 23 -> max (1.3130), 2.5 / 23 -> step. The view starts at max (spawn and respawn); the wheel steps it by step per notch between min and max. ctrl: holding Ctrl (Sneak) eases the view to max x ctrl, the same 52.5 m of ground across it showed before (46.4 m back at the data's lens). glide_m: metres added to the distance under the glider (the data's +5.81 m of arm). abyss: below the lip of the map the arm grows from add_from_m at from_m deep to add_to_m at to_m deep and stays there (the data's +0.5..+15 m over 3.5..10 m), off for falls shorter than from_m. omega: rad/s of the critically damped spring the arm length follows (the match only; the farm eases its zoom as before). cap: the widest the view ever goes, with the glider and height stacked on top.

source.fov_note: 35.3 is the target feel data (a 59 degree horizontal lens at 16:9); the footage read 25-34 before the data was known
source.across_note: 34.0 is the target feel data (34.2 m: a 30.2 m arm at a 59 degree horizontal lens); the footage read 35-39 m
